title: YOUNG ENTREPRENEURS
subtitle: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
passage:
A growing number of school-going teenagers are using the internet to [[0]] their pocket money by selling clothes and accessories online. One shopping app has over seven million users worldwide, [[1]] many enterprising under-18s who have decided they would [[2]] work for themselves than look for a part-time job in a shop or restaurant.

Sixteen-year-old Eva Laidlaw, who has [[3]] up in a family of successful business people, buys second-hand garments then sells them via the app, more [[4]] than not, at a decent profit. ‘I get most of my clothes from charity shops and car boot sales,’ she says. ‘You can [[5]] across good quality items if you're [[6]] to spend the time looking.’

Katie Simmons is another young entrepreneur. [[7]] on holiday in Tuscany three years ago, she discovered that clothes sold in the markets there were extremely cheap. So, every two months, Katie, now eighteen, [[8]] for Italy and hunts for items she thinks will sell easily at home. ‘I had intended to go to uni,’ says Katie, ‘but now I have a business to run.’

items.explainCorrect: **Including** introduces examples among the users — under-18s are part of that group.

explainIfChosen.0: **Containing** usually needs a physical container — odd after *users worldwide*.
explainIfChosen.3: **Introducing** would mean presenting new people — not listing who the users include.

items.explainCorrect: **Would rather** + bare infinitive + *than* — preference: work for themselves than look for a job.

explainIfChosen.0: **Would better** is not a structure (*had better* is different).
explainIfChosen.1: **Would prefer** needs *to* work / *working* — not *prefer work … than*.
explainIfChosen.2: **Would like** needs *to* + infinitive — not *like work … than*.

items.explainCorrect: **Grown up** = spent childhood — *has grown up in a family*.

explainIfChosen.0: **Turned up** means arrived / appeared — wrong meaning.
explainIfChosen.2: **Brought up** needs an object (*was brought up*) — not *has brought up in*.
explainIfChosen.3: **Raised up** is not the phrasal; *was raised* is passive without *up* here.

items.explainCorrect: Fixed phrase **more often than not** = usually / most of the time.

explainIfChosen.1: **More ever than not** is not English.
explainIfChosen.2: **More always than not** is not the idiom.
explainIfChosen.3: **More sometimes than not** is not the fixed phrase.

items.explainCorrect: **Come across** = find by chance while looking.

explainIfChosen.0: **Get across** means communicate an idea — wrong meaning.
explainIfChosen.1: **Find across** is not a phrasal verb.
explainIfChosen.3: **Take across** is not the collocation here.

items.explainCorrect: **Prepared to** + infinitive = willing to (spend the time looking).

explainIfChosen.1: **Disposed to** needs a different pattern and meaning (inclined).
explainIfChosen.3: **Equipped to** means having tools/skills — less natural than *prepared to* for willingness.

items.explainCorrect: **While on holiday** = during the time she was on holiday.

explainIfChosen.0: **Whereas** contrasts two facts — she is not contrasting here.
explainIfChosen.1: **Whenever** means every time — she discovered it once on that holiday.
explainIfChosen.3: **Whether on holiday** needs an alternative (*whether … or …*).

items.explainCorrect: **Set off for** a place = start a journey towards it.

explainIfChosen.0: **Goes away for Italy** is unnatural (*goes away to*).
explainIfChosen.2: **Carries on for Italy** is not a travel collocation.
explainIfChosen.3: **Catches up for Italy** is wrong (*catch up with* someone).
